BSD: A SINGLE-LINE / LONG RECTANGLE license plate. Aspect ratio clearly wider than tall (width / height ≥ ≈3). All characters on ONE row. Often seen on car front bumpers, long European-style plates, or long-format Vietnamese plates. If the plate is squarish (two rows of characters) → BSV. If aspect ratio is ambiguous → unknown.
BSV: A TWO-LINE / SQUARE license plate. Aspect ratio roughly square (width / height < ≈2). Characters split into TWO rows. Common on motorbikes, rear of cars in some regions, and Vietnamese rear plates. If only one row of characters and plate is clearly elongated → BSD. If row count is ambiguous → unknown.
human: A single pedestrian — body visible without any vehicle frame attached. Strict pixel evidence required: NO motorbike/bicycle wheel, handlebar, fuel tank, or seat touching the body in the crop. If the bike is cropped out of frame but the person is fully visible (no body part suggests they were ON a bike) → human. If any wheel/handlebar/seat/tank touches the person → motorbike_with_driver / bike_with_driver. Person inside a car/bus does NOT count → unknown.
sedan: Passenger car with a 3-BOX SILHOUETTE: engine bay / cabin / separate trunk. Includes 4-door sedans, 2-door coupes (treat as sedans), convertibles with top up, and station wagons (3-box silhouette with a longer roof and separate rear door — still sedan, not hatchback). Roof clearly slopes to a rear deck OR a long flat roof with a separate vertical rear door. Car-like ride height (not tall like SUV). NOT a hatchback (which has steep rear flush from roof to bumper) and NOT a pickup (no open cargo bed). If trunk/rear structure is unclear → unknown.
hatchback: 5-door passenger car with REAR HATCH flush from roof to bumper, no separate trunk bump. Steep rear window angle continues into the cargo door. Compact size, two visible side doors per side. If rear shape isn't clearly hatch-style → unknown.
suv: Tall passenger 4-wheeler with HIGH RIDE HEIGHT and large fender arches. Body height ≈ width; bulky. Includes crossovers / CUVs (compact SUVs like CR-V, Innova, Xpander, Fortuner) — basically any car-shaped vehicle taller than a hatchback. NOT a pickup (no open cargo bed). NOT a hatchback (clearly taller, larger wheel arches). NOT a passenger van (vans are box-shaped with flat sides; SUVs have sloped/curved sides). If body height is car-like (low ride) → hatchback or sedan. If box-shaped with flat slab sides → bus_m (passenger van) or truck_m.
pickup: Light-duty truck with VISIBLE OPEN CARGO BED behind the cab. Cab has 2-4 doors; bed has tailgate. Bed walls clearly lower than cab roof. If bed is enclosed/covered with no opening visible → unknown.
bus_m: Medium passenger vehicle, box-shaped with FLAT SLAB SIDES and a row of side windows. Includes single-deck buses ≈8–10m / 2 axles, minibuses, microbuses, and passenger vans (Hi-Ace, Solati, Mercedes V-Class, Sprinter passenger, Transit passenger, Vito). Key cue: clearly a passenger carrier (multiple side windows for seating), upright slab-sided body, NOT an SUV (which has sloped sides) and NOT a cargo van (which has solid panel sides without rear windows). NOT articulated (no bend in middle). If clearly long ≥11m or 3+ axles → bus_l/bus_xl. If a cargo van with solid panel sides and no rear windows → truck_m.
bus_l: Single-deck bus, LARGE length (≈11–13m, 2 or 3 axles). Long rectangular body, many side windows. NOT articulated, NOT a city minibus. If articulated → bus_xl. If short (<10m) → bus_m.
bus_xl: Extra-long bus: ARTICULATED with a flexible joint in the middle, OR coach >13m with 3 axles and luggage bay. Clear visual cue: middle bellows joint, OR very long single rigid body. If <13m and rigid → bus_l.
truck_m: Medium commercial / utility vehicle, 2 axles, with an enclosed cargo box, open flatbed, or special body behind the cab. Includes cargo vans with solid panel sides and no rear windows (panel Sprinter, Transit cargo), light box trucks, refrigerated trucks, ambulances (van-style), small fire trucks, garbage trucks of medium size, tow trucks, food trucks, utility/service trucks. Smaller than a semi-tractor; NO trailer. Wheelbase shorter than a city bus. If a passenger version with side windows → bus_m. If 3+ axles, articulated, or with trailer → truck_l/truck_xl. If a parked trailer alone with no cab visible → truck_l based on length.
truck_l: Large rigid truck, 3 axles (rigid body, no separate trailer) OR a small tractor + short trailer combo. Visible double-rear-axle group. Includes large fire engines, large garbage trucks, cement mixers, large dump trucks, large tow trucks. Includes parked semi-trailers seen alone (without a cab) when length is moderate. If clearly a tractor + full container / semi-trailer / fuel tanker → truck_xl. If 2 axles only → truck_m.
truck_xl: Extra-large truck: TRACTOR + SEMI-TRAILER (articulated) OR tractor + container / fuel tanker / car carrier / lowboy. 4+ axles total, separation between cab and cargo unit clearly visible. If single rigid body (no separation between cab and cargo) → truck_l/truck_m. If the crop is just the parked long trailer without a cab → truck_l (the separating cab is the key cue for truck_xl).
twowheels_standalone: A two-wheeled vehicle (bicycle, motorbike, scooter) WITHOUT a visible rider in the crop. Also includes parked three-wheeled motorbike-cargo carts (xe ba gác) with no driver visible. Strict pixel evidence: empty seat, no human leg straddling, no body part touching the bike. If the rider is cropped out of frame and only the bike is visible, this is the correct label — DO NOT infer a rider you can't see. If any body part (leg, hand, torso) is contacting the bike → motorbike_with_driver or bike_with_driver. If both bike and a person are partially visible but no contact point is in the crop → unknown.
motorbike_with_driver: A MOTORBIKE (engine block, fuel tank between knees, twist throttle, often muffler) with a rider in physical contact: at least one of {leg straddling the tank, body seated on the seat, hands on handlebars} MUST be visible inside the crop. Also INCLUDES: scooters with a step-through frame (Vespa-style, Honda Wave/Vision/Lead), motorbikes with a rear passenger or rear cargo box, 3-wheeled motorbike-cargo vehicles (xe ba gác — motorbike front with a rear cargo tray and 2 rear wheels), tuk-tuks (a single rider/driver controlling a motorcycle-style front with a passenger compartment behind), and motorbikes carrying loose cargo. The defining cue: a powered two-or-three-wheeler with an engine AND a human in physical contact with it. NOT a bicycle (no engine, only pedals). Edge-occlusion rule: if the rider is cropped out of frame and no body part contacts the bike in the crop → twowheels_standalone. If the bike is cropped out and only the person is visible → human. If bicycle pedals visible and no engine → bike_with_driver. Genuine ambiguity (tiny crop, both heavily occluded) → unknown.
bike_with_driver: A BICYCLE (pedals, chain, thin frame tubing, NO engine block, NO fuel tank) with a rider in physical contact: at least one of {foot on pedal, body seated on the seat, hand on handlebar} MUST be visible inside the crop. Edge-occlusion rule: if the rider is cropped out of frame and no body part contacts the bike in the crop → twowheels_standalone. If the bike is cropped out and only the person is visible → human. If an engine block or fuel tank is visible → motorbike_with_driver. Genuine ambiguity (tiny crop, both heavily occluded) → unknown.
